content.label: I have used this app for several years and upgraded to the paid version. I purchased the app to help aggregate data in ways that the Apple Watch doesn’t. I don’t always use the exercise mode but would still my workout recorded. The data is easily available.

The way this app pushed me to do more and more beyond my limits could’ve injured me. Instead, it just made me depressed and feeling like a slacker. No workout was ever good enough for this app, even burning 900 calories swimming for over an hour. It still wanted more! That day! Then it crashed my progress the next day and we’re in the midst of a major heat wave. I’d faint if I did what this app wanted. One day I did 3 workouts and that wasn’t enough either! Had to delete this app and not get the benefit of what I paid for just for my mental health. Welltory is what this app aimed to be and failed miserably. What sort of “gentler” app encourages burnout!

Good to start, and I enjoyed it for a while. However as I have gotten more into the gym I’ve found this to be a bit too gentle. I feel I rest appropriately and I have split training days, so an app telling me to take it easy when I know I can handle an arm day when I did legs or core the day before just isn’t helpful anymore.
I absolutely love this app. I need a general habit tracker in this same vibe.

For me, it’s rare to find an app that isn’t just a cheap cash grab. This app, is one of those rare moments. 

It’s not often I get to write a genuine five-star review, but Gentler Streak proved itself to be extremely useful and helpful. Not only does it break down exercise stats into metrics I can actually understand, but it also encourages you to be more active if you haven’t done much lately. On the other hand, it also lets you know when you should tone it down a bit if you’re pushing too hard, even recommending easier workouts called “Going Gentler” (currently, I am not using a subscription, so I don’t actually know how good these workout recommendations are). 

Another thing I thought worth mentioning was its compatibility with the Apple Health and Fitness apps. If the user allows, Gentler Streak can use data from Health like sleep data, steps, breathing quality, etc. As another plus, whatever exercises you record using Gentler Streak’s Apple Watch app will count towards Apple’s own Fitness app, used for closing your Fitness Rings and such. Very useful! Now I won’t have to track my exercises on both Gentler Streak and Apple Fitness.

In short: Gentler Streak has become a necessity for my workouts, and has proven to surpass my expectations. Using the Apple Watch app to track my workouts is extremely user-friendly (pretty much everything useful on this app needs an Apple Watch to track workouts, so only get this if you have an Apple Watch). The message when you open the app is encouraging and helpful, and has motivated me to continue on my fitness journey. Easy five stars.

title.label: A Lifesaver for Chronic Illness Warriors

content.label:
As someone living with lupus, fatigue, and joint pain, I’ve tried so many health and fitness apps over the years hoping one would finally “get me.” Most either pushed too hard or made me feel guilty for not keeping up. But then I found Gentler Streak, and I genuinely thank God for this app.

Gentler Streak is unlike anything I’ve ever used. It doesn’t just track your activity, it understands your limits. It let me know when I was overextending myself and even told me how many days I should rest to recover. That kind of care is rare in the world of fitness apps, where the default is “go harder or go home.”

It tracks my sleep, heart rate, and other metrics in a simple, beautiful interface. But my favorite feature? It actually counts household chores as a workout. Like finally! Yes, scrubbing, lifting, and cleaning while managing a flare does count!

Gentler Streak nudges me to stay consistent without shaming me. On days when all I can manage is a five-minute stretch, it encourages me. That kind of grace makes a world of difference.

And now with the new update, steps count toward our fitness journey! This is exactly what I’ve been missing. Some days, I don’t do a formal workout but take wayyy too many steps and end up completely burned out. Now those steps are recognized, and I can pace myself better. This update makes Gentler Streak even more amazing for people like me. (Just a side note, it would be great if a future update could include the perceived exertion for steps as on the workouts!)

I don’t usually buy apps, but I gladly purchased this one. It’s not just a fitness tracker, it’s a compassionate wellness companion for people like me who want to care for their bodies without burning out.

Thank you, Gentler Streak, for meeting me where I am and helping me stay strong, gently.

title.label: Wish I could measure cardio fitness in a gym

content.label: Apple health does not support measuring cardio fitness using gym equipment, I was hoping gentler streak would add this measurement.

I have issues with post-exercise malaise. This app was promoted to me as a perfect fit for my needs. I was told that, through my Apple Watch, the app would figure out a good starting and stopping point for me. It is not. You have to record an exercise routine for seven days in a row before it will calculate anything.

The developer response less that helpful. I’ve had my watch for almost a year and the app had access to that data. I’m not supposed to do workouts because of my post-exercise malaise.

I am so glad that this app has helped so many people; however, I haven’t had the same experience in the month I’ve used it. The app doesn’t seem to be content with my activity (aka consider my activity as improving my fitness level) unless I’m weightlifting for an hour, plus running for 30-60 minutes, plus walking for an hour or two in a single day, and the only time it recommends me taking a rest day is when I pull an all-nighter or get about 4 hours of sleep. When I finally get the sleep I need, it wants me to “push forward” that day rather than actually recover. I just think that for me personally it’s better for me to pick my own rest days, as the app could leave me to overexert myself. Maybe that will change after continuing to use the app for a longer stretch of time!

title.label: Frozen heart rate on mirrored workout

content.label: I use the Gentler app with a chest heart rate monitor and start workouts from my Apple Watch in Gentler app. The heart rate is displayed correctly on the watch itself, but there’s an issue: when the watch goes into inactive mode (the workout time still shows, but without milliseconds), the current heart rate readings stop being transmitted to the iPhone — the mirrored workout screen shows a frozen heart rate. To get the iPhone to display the current data again, I have to tap the watch screen to bring back the display with milliseconds. It would be great if heart rate data were transmitted to the iPhone consistently, regardless of the watch screen state.

The gentler option gives me a suitable reference indicator, like the progress bar on the homepage, which helps me understand whether I’ve met my daily exercise goals or if I haven’t done enough. It allows me to arrange my life easily and prevents me from overexerting myself and causing muscle strains.

Also, the Apple Watch is compatible, but I prefer to stay consistent with Fitness+ and use Apple's official fitness app. I don’t have any other reason for this preference. However, I have to say that it offers many features, and most of them are free. As a student, I don't have much pocket money and can't afford the premium version. The app is easy to use and very self explanatory. I like the menstrual tracking and telling me when to take it easy during each cycle. I also love the articles for all sorts of topics, the wellbeing section, and the sleep information. 

I know I have self discipline to work out and eat well but I didn’t really have a set path, with this app I feel like I’m able to set a path for myself and see my progress overtime. I love the monthly insights, showing me what zone I was in during my workout, the notes, and telling me when it should be a rest day and when I need to pick up the pace and work towards my goals. 

All in all, this app is amazing and i love seeing my progress overtime time.
